summary: Chijun Hamada was a Buddhist studies scholar. In 1978, he held posts as an assistant at Taisho University and as a researcher at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute.

Chikafumi Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a master's degree at the University of British Columbia and a PhD at the University of Calgary, studying under Leslie S. Kawamura, Ashok Aklujkar, and Karin Preisendanz, among others.
Chiko Corona is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued traditional training under Kenkō Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura.
Chikyo Yamamoto (1913–1999) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served at Koyasan University as a professor, attested in 1970, and later as a part-time lecturer, attested in 1980.
Chime Rinpoche (1941–2026) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Gangshar. He held a position at the British Library from circa 1973 to 1985.

Chin Kung (1927–2022) was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy scholar. He founded the Hwa Dzan Buddhist Library and Corporate Body of the Buddha Educational Foundation, led the Pure Land Learning College Association (~2001–2022), and held multiple professorships.

Ching Keng is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He earned a PhD from Harvard University (~2003–2009) under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, also studying at UT Austin. Around 2011, he became an associate professor at National Chengchi University.

Ching-mei Shyu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed an MA under Jan Nattier at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and earned a PhD from Cornell University in 2008 under Daniel Boucher and Hubert Durt.

Chintaharan Chakravarti (1900–1972) was an Indology scholar who served as a professor at Presidency University. He also held posts at Bethune College, attested in 1941, and served as publication secretary at Sanskrit Sahitya Parishat, attested in 1960.

Chintaman Ganesh Kashikar (1910–2007) was an Indologist. He served as assistant secretary at the Vaidika Samshodhana Mandala, attested in 1941, and later held a professorship at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.
Chirapat Prapandvidya (born 1941) is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He founded Silpakorn University and served as its director in 1996.

Chisan Kohō (1879–1967) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and Kyodo Koshuin. He founded Tsurumi Women's University in 1966 and served in leadership roles at Saijō-ji, Nagano Ken Senmon Nisodo, and Sōji-ji (~1957–1967).
Chisei Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He held positions at Mampuku-ji Bunkaden, where he is attested from 2003 and served as director as attested in 2006.

Chitai Takenaka (born 1945) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1964–1968). He served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (attested 1979–1983) and as a professor at Tokoha University (attested 1989).

Chizen Akanuma (1884–1937) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kōkōdō and Otani University. He co-founded the Eastern Buddhist Society in 1921 and was a professor at Otani University in 1919.

Chizuko Yoshimizu (born 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She completed a doctorate at the University of Vienna (1990–1994) and was appointed lecturer (2003), associate professor (2008), and professor (2011) at the University of Tsukuba.

Chlodwig H. Werba (born 1947) is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He has been affiliated with the University of Vienna, where he served as professor, attested between 1990 and 2022.
Chogye Shabdrung (born 1981) is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sakya College in 2003 under Khenchen Sonam Gyatso.

Chogye Trichen Rinpoche (1920–2007) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure. He studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Geshe Tsechok, and Kunga Chophel, and became the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Phenpo Nalendra Monastery in 1928.

Chogyū Takayama (1871–1902) was a scholar in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Fukushima Prefectural Asaka High School from circa 1888 to 1891 and at the University of Tokyo from circa 1893 to 1896.
